memory_update.text: SPSC is the highest-priority underfollowed pure-play for the retail trading-partner network node; verify latest retention, recurring revenue, trading-partner count, and small-supplier churn before promoting beyond Layer 1.

OTEX may hide a scaled B2B commerce-network asset inside a broader enterprise information-management company; later layers should isolate Business Network exposure rather than using consolidated OpenText metrics.
DSGX is a less pure but relevant logistics-network adjacency; its GLN, EDI, customs, and ecommerce connectivity may make it a second-order beneficiary of retail supplier complexity.

Several direct EDI/trading-partner assets are private or no longer separately public, including TrueCommerce, CommerceHub/Rithum, 1WorldSync/Syndigo-style product data networks, and E2open after its 2025 WiseTech acquisition.

summary: Expanded the universe around retail EDI, trading-partner enablement, compliance workflows, and supplier connectivity. The cleanest pure-play found is SPS Commerce, while OpenText and Descartes provide broader B2B/logistics-network exposure that may be under-modeled as consumer-retail infrastructure. IBM Sterling is included only as a reference anchor because it validates the enterprise-grade EDI/VAN bottleneck but is too diversified and mega-cap to be a primary underfollowed candidate.
